findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be kept past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following TCS items to be hot held below 135F:
(Repeat) 1) Queso to be hot held at 70F. 
2) Rice to be hot held at 110F.

Discussed with PIC, queso and rice was moved to stovetop and reheated to 165F. Ensure any TCS food being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to missing date marking in multiple coolers and walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, items were prepared before the 7 day date marking maximum so proper date marking was placed on items. Ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed beef/steaks to be improperly thawing outside of cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper thawing practices and beef was moved to walk in cooler. Ensure when thawing, any TCS item is placed in a cooler or under running water.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed onions in dry storage room to be resting directly on floor. Discussed with PIC, items were removed from floor and placed at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any food items is at least 6 inches off of ground.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed clean utensils to not be inverted. Discussed with PIC, utensil were put through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process and inverted. Ensure any cleaned utensils are inverted to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed kitchen line prep coolers to be soiled with food debris under lids. Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Observed leak to be present under fan unit in walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, leak will be serviced. A container was placed under leak to contain it, ensure walk in cooler is working to meet manufactures standards.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed food handler training to be missing for some members of staff. Discussed with PIC, remaining staff members will receive license. Ensure any food handling employee has completed the required food handlers training within 30 days of hiring. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed CFM on duty to not have allergen training completed. DIscussed with PIC, training will be completed. Ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handlers licenses to be present upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure any member of staff that handles food completes food handlers training and that licenses are kept within facility at all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed no certified food protection manager available. Ensure the facility has 1-3 certified food protection manager’s to cover all hours of operation. Correct by the next routine inspection.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers to not have any date marking available. Discussed with PIC. Ensure any TCS foods kept longer than 24 hours are properly date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers with white colored powders to not have proper labels. Discussed with PIC, ensure any white colored powders not kept in original container is correctly labelled. 

3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed utensils being stored handle facing down. Discussed with PIC, ensure utensils are being stored in a capacity that prevents contamination. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.
